leverage.exposure: This is the item that outranks everything else in the briefing. There is a live offer on the Freiburg left-back that exceeds available cash, and the sale meant to fund it has not been made. A Kickbase board listing resolves at expiry rather than on a seller's whim, so nothing can land tonight — but it resolves only a couple of hours before the matchday lock, which is a very thin window in which to sell a defender and get back to positive. A negative balance when the matchday starts scores zero for the entire matchday, so this is not a rounding risk, it is the whole matchday. Raising the bid without selling Bernardo first makes the hole deeper, not shallower. Sell first, then raise — the previous run gave the same instruction and the order got inverted, which is exactly how the Lienhart position came about.

binding_gap: The binding constraint is no longer squad size, it is sequencing. The squad is legal and can field its optimal shape today. What binds is that the funding sale, the listing that must be pulled, and the bid that must be raised all have to happen in the right order, and two of the three have not happened yet.

verdict.headline: Georg acted on the last briefing but only halfway, and the half he skipped is the one that carries the risk.
verdict.headline_short: Georg acted on the last briefing but only halfway, and the half he ski
verdict.detail: Georg acted on the last briefing but only halfway, and the half he skipped is the one that carries the risk. The Makengo bid is live — good — but it was placed well below the figure that was called for, and it was placed BEFORE the Bernardo sale rather than after. So the squad now sits with an offer outstanding that is larger than the cash behind it, on a player the ledger wants, at a price the measured market says will lose. Both halves of that need fixing, and in a specific order: pull the Amoako listing, sell Bernardo, then raise the Makengo bid. Nothing else on the board is worth a slot. Separately, the Lienhart scare from the last run resolved itself harmlessly while nobody was looking — he went to a rival and Georg's cash was never touched.

sell.reason: Bernardo remains the sale, and the case is the same one the ledger settled after flipping on him three times: not a confirmed injury, not a confirmed benching, but flagged knocked-up by Kickbase since the Cologne away game and hooked at just past the hour in the only match he has played. This run's independent sweep found him absent from the injury table and included in a same-day projected eleven, which is consistent with that read rather than contradicting it — the projection appears to be derived from his last lineup rather than from fresh team news, and Kickbase's own status flag is both newer and first-party. The selling edge is that his market value is still rising, so the flag is not priced in yet, and that edge decays. Widmer stays a hold, not a sale: he is confirmed a substitute rather than a starter, but he is also the last spare defensive body, and selling him raises almost nothing while risking a penalty. Lokonga stays a keeper — his blocked-list entry still describes him as a funding leg for a trade that no longer exists, and that text is stale.

standing.why: REPLACES Sr72ldn (closed). THE SALE IS UNCHANGED; THE REASON FOR IT IS CORRECTED, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS BECAUSE THE LEDGER HAS NOW FLIPPED ON THIS PLAYER THREE TIMES. Do not re-cite Sr72ldn's claim that he is "confirmed out of the Hoffenheim XI, HRANAC at left-back" - it does not survive re-fetching. Three reads of one page, three different elevens. TREAT LIGAINSIDER CLUB-PAGE XI EXTRACTION AS UNRELIABLE - see the companion HOLD. THE EVIDENCE THAT ACTUALLY DECIDES IT is Kickbase's own status text, which no previous run pulled: get_player 1954 returns st 2, stl [2], stxt "Stricken - does not come through KOE (A) unscathed", dt 2026-08-31T14:40:12Z. That is an INJURY DOUBT arising from the Koeln away game, not a benching - the precise opposite of what Sr72ldn concluded, and it is first-party rather than a scraped graphic. It corroborates the one mechanical fact nobody disputes: in Koeln 3:2 Hoffenheim, 29.08.2026 he started at left-back and was HOOKED AT 53 MINUTES with a rating of 4.0 (sec 3268). SO THE CORRECT READ IS: not confirmed benched, not confirmed injured, but flagged knocked-up by Kickbase since 31.08 and pulled at half-time-plus-8 in the only match he has played. His ap 62 is a doubt, not an expectation. He is NOT on Ligainsider's Verletzte-und-Gesperrte table (checked 03.09.2026 - Hoffenheim has no entries at all) and his Ligainsider profile box reads green fit, so do NOT report him as a confirmed injury either. WHY SELL ANYWAY, AND THE CASE IS STRONGER THAN THE OLD ONE: (1) his mv has TURNED UP - mv 7.048.552, mvt 1, tfhmvt +160.481, sdmvt +218.838 - so the market has priced neither the st 2 flag nor the 53-minute hook. Selling a flagged player into a rising price is a seller's edge and it decays. (2) At 11 players there is zero spare, so a fielded man who might not play is a fielded ZERO with no bench cover - keeping him is not the safe option, it is the risky one. (3) THE MONEY IS THE POINT: this sale is the gate on the Makengo buy. Cash is 4.107.522 and the Makengo bid needs ~9.000.000; only this sale unlocks it. EXECUTE FIRST, AFTER PULLING THE AMOAKO LISTING: 12 -> 11 = 1GK/4DEF/4MID/2ATT which fills 4-4-2 legally, cash -> 11.156.074, and the run's whole plan is funded. Sell to the board at mv 7.048.552 - do not list him at a premium, there is no time and a st 2 flag will not clear one. REVERSAL: a source dated 03.09.2026 or later putting him in the Hoffenheim XI for the Dortmund home game AND the Kickbase st flag clearing to 0. The flag clearing alone is not enough, and neither is another Ligainsider read.

buy.reason: Makengo is the buy and the case has not weakened — a full ninety minutes at left-back on the opening day, fit, in the projected eleven, the transfer interest in him publicly withdrawn, and the German window shut so he cannot leave before the matchday. He is comfortably the best points-per-euro asset the board has produced, and the trade is robust in both directions: if Bernardo is fine it is a modest gain, and if Bernardo's flag turns into a blank it is a large one. The problem is the price on the offer. Georg's live bid sits barely above market value, and every contested Kickbase board listing this ledger has measured has cleared far above that — including two fresh ones settled today, both landing squarely in the middle of the band. The fact that the listing shows no rival offer right now is not reassurance: it has more than a day left to run, and what matters is who is bidding at expiry, not who is bidding now. Raise it into the measured band. This is not the Onyeka mistake in reverse — that was paying an outlier premium on a listing nobody else wanted; this is declining to bid inside a band that seven separate clearings have now mapped. Nothing else on the board earns a look: the one substantial new listing is a Leverkusen defender whose points-per-euro is roughly five times worse, and taking him would force a second sale that surrenders more fielded points than it buys.
